stories.notes: Complex multi-platform CMS live preview feature with empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Assigning both agents: openspec first to elaborate requirements and add technical depth for real-time rendering across GO/UP/MX platforms, then speckit to harden testability, security, and edge-case coverage. High priority due to complexity and complete lack of AC.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. The attachment point is useContent, the central hook consumed by 236+ components. All downstream Contentstack components (ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, etc.) would automatically render draft content once useContent (or its underlying client) routes requests to Contentstack's preview API when preview parameters are present. Acceptance criteria are empty; VCs derived from the description alone.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria with valuable architectural context. I authored the full AC list from scratch based on the story description, technical notes, and file paths. Key areas covered: (1) Core happy path — draft content returned with preview params, published content without (AC-1, AC-2). (2) Propagation through ContentstackContext → useContent → downstream components (AC-3). (3) Error handling — API failures, invalid/expired params, fallback behavior (AC-4, AC-5). (4) Security — no token/key leakage in client bundles (AC-6). (5) Observable indicator for editors (AC-7). (6) Navigation persistence of preview mode (AC-8). (7) Edge cases — no draft version exists (AC-9), exiting preview mode (AC-10), concurrent requests (AC-11), filtered preview params (AC-12), missing context provider (AC-13). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: File contents were not available for review. ACs are derived solely from the story title, description, file paths, and openspec's notes. If the actual implementation of useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts, or ContentstackLink.tsx reveals existing preview-related logic, some ACs may need adjustment.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec provided architectural context (identifying useContent as the central attachment point consumed by 236+ components, and explaining downstream propagation through ContentstackContext), while speckit authored a comprehensive AC list (AC-1 through AC-13) covering happy path, propagation, error handling, security, observability, and edge cases. However, two concerns require human review: (1) openspec did not fulfill its primary mandate of AC elaboration — it left acceptance criteria empty (acceptanceChanged: false) and deferred all AC authoring to speckit, which is a pipeline role gap; (2) speckit explicitly caveated that file contents (useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx) were not available, meaning all ACs are derived from the story description and openspec's notes alone. If actual implementation reveals existing preview-related logic, ACs may need adjustment. The collaborative output is solid but carries unresolved assumption risk that a human should validate before implementation.
